findings.evidence:
`field--invalid`, a red border (`#e5484d`); the list of errors at the top of
the page is removed, since the red border already shows where the problem
is. No message text is added, to keep the form compact.
findings.recommendation: Keep a text error message for each invalid field, rendered next to the field and associated with it through `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid="true"` on the input (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, 3.3.1 Error Identification, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value). A screen reader user who tabs out of the postcode field with `ABC` hears nothing, and a colour-blind user cannot tell the red border from the grey one; neither learns which field is wrong or why (the existing messages from `rules.ts`, e.g. `postcodeError`, already give the text). Update the spec scenarios "An invalid postcode" and "A corrected field" to require the message text and its association, not only the border colour, and task 1.2 accordingly.
findings.title: Field errors are conveyed by colour only, with no text message

findings.evidence: - The error list at the top of the form is removed.
findings.recommendation: Today `web/src/checkout/Form.tsx:22` renders the errors in a `<div role="alert" className="error-summary">`, which a screen reader announces on submit. The plan removes it and says nothing about what happens when the customer presses Pay with invalid or untouched fields: a keyboard or screen reader user who presses Pay gets no announcement and no focus change, so the payment simply does not happen without explanation (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 4.1.3 Status Messages). Specify the submit behaviour: either keep the summary (with `role="alert"` and links to the fields) or move focus to the first invalid field whose message is associated with it; add a scenario for submitting with an invalid field.
findings.title: Removing the error summary leaves a failed submit silent
